This appeal coming on for admission this day, th e court  following:
 ORDER

This is first criminal appeal under Section 14-a sub section (2) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act (hereinafter referred to as "SC/ST Act") filed by the appellant assailing the order dated 06.03.2024 passed by Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Ashoknagar (M.P.) whereby, application preferred by the appellant herein under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. relating to Crime No. 32 of 2024 registered at Police Station Naisarai, District Ashoknagar (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 376, 376 (D), 376 (2) (n), 506 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(w) (ii), 3 (2) (v), 3 (2)
(va) of the SC/ST Act has been rejected.

Learned counsel for the appellant argued that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
Allegedly the incident occurred between 11.11.2023 to 17.01.2024.
The prosecutrix is a major married woman, however, there is no evidence that she lodged any report or made complaint to her husband who was alongwith her during this period about the incident.
No plausible explanation has been given for delay in lodging F.I.R. which is lodged on 17.01.2024 after gap of almost three months.
It is further submitted that the case is not supported by medical evidence as well as DNA report is not found corroborative.
The appellant is under custody since 28.02.2024.
The appellant is having no criminal history.

After conclusion of investigation, charge sheet has already been filed,
therefore, his custodial interrogation is not required anymore.
Further argument is that appellant is the permanent resident of District Ashoknagar (M.P.) and there is no possibility of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
Hence, he prays for grant of bail to the appellant.
Per contra, learned Panel Lawyer for respondent No.1/State vehemently opposed the appeal and prayed for its rejection.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting upon the merits of the case, this appeal stands allowed and it is directed that the appellant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rs. Two Lakh Only) with two solvent sureties of Rs.1,00,000/- each in the like amount each to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court/Committal Court.

This order will remain operative subject to compliance of the following conditions by the appellant:-
1.
The appellant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
Learned State counsel is directed to send an e-copy of this order to the Station House Officer of the concerned Police Station for information and necessary action.
